clue.text: Son, upper-class type, and bishop needing no work to become snooty

parts.note: a nob is an informal word for a toff, a person of high social rank

indicators.note: needing no means the following word for work is dropped from bishop

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A haughty family of a son, a toff and an idle bishop looking down on everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no' drops OP from BISHOP, leaving BISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbish and snooty are synonyms, both describing a person who looks down on others.

clue.text: I will interrupt passage in church, being artless

indicators.note: will interrupt says the letter I breaks into the word that follows

parts.note: the nave is the central passage or aisle of a church

explanation.surface: Someone vows to break into the walk down the church aisle, innocently unaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' looks like I'LL, but I is the piece and 'will interrupt' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive and artless are synonyms meaning innocent and lacking guile.

clue.text: Support record showing work not yet completed

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a log is a written record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A supporting document reveals the pile of unfinished jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of tasks still waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Unwell still, though losing stone

indicators.note: losing tells us the abbreviation for stone is taken away from the word still

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A patient is still poorly despite shedding some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, fourteen pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill and unwell are synonyms for being in poor health.

clue.text: Last pair of gardeners in gardens attack the weeds? That's a lucky thing

indicators.note: in places those two letters inside the word for gardens

parts.note: hoes, as a verb, means works the garden soil with a hoe

parts.note: to hoe is to cut up weeds with a hoe

explanation.surface: Gardeners hacking at weeds count themselves fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb here, not a noun: one who gardens works the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: Imitate policeman going to Yard

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A copycat officer heads off to Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' hints at Scotland Yard, London police headquarters, but is only the abbreviation Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to imitate or mimic them.

clue.text: Company gathered together to find astronomical object

parts.note: people who met have gathered together

explanation.surface: A firm's staff assemble for a night of stargazing.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body orbiting the sun, a classic sight in the night sky.

clue.text: Ridicule medicine, or remedy, finally

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word remedy

explanation.surface: Mocking a cure: a tablet or some other remedy at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory someone is to subject them to public scorn, as in the old wooden pillory.

clue.text: Some editor-in-chief is calling regarding the Treasury

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss is on the phone about government finances.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle chieF IS CALling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal means relating to public revenue, which the Treasury manages.

clue.text: Discover truth about complaint — not good

indicators.note: not says the letter for good must be removed from the complaint word

parts.note: a grumble is a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone uncovers what lies behind an unpleasant grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to rumble someone is to see through them or find out their secret.

clue.text: Get a sense of payment left

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: Someone senses there is still a charge outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something is to sense or perceive it.

clue.text: Item for discussion is not quite lacking it, somehow

indicators.note: lacking says the letters of the word it are missing from the jumbled pool
somehow signals that the remaining letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A debating point is almost there but missing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes I and T from IS NOT QUITE, and the anagram signal rearranges the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A question is a matter raised for debate, as in the question before the meeting.

clue.text: Peevish Queen reformed rule over America

indicators.note: reformed means the word rule is shaped into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A grumpy monarch reshapes rule over the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Querulous means complaining in a petulant way, much the same as peevish.

clue.text: Criminal attempt recalled in regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker remembers a failed try with remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, close to a criminal.

clue.text: Criticise return of routine: source of eventual happiness

indicators.note: return of means the word for routine is read backwards

explanation.surface: Knocking a return to the daily grind ends, eventually, in joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a state of intense joy, an extreme form of happiness.

clue.text: One of Snow White's dwarfs very quietly brought in grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass
PP is pianissimo, the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A dwarf from the fairy tale is quietly carried in on some hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White, alongside Doc and Grumpy.

clue.text: Variety of plait seen around one girl's head?

definitions.text: Variety of plait seen around one girl's head?

Variety of means the letters of plait are made into another variety

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of the word girl's

explanation.surface: A style of braid on a girl's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges PLAIT around I and G; the whole clue also describes a pigtail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigtail is a braid of hair hanging from the back or side of the head.

clue.text: A quiet intermission around end of recital — then this erupts?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: around says the pause word surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: a pause is a break or intermission

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word recital

explanation.surface: After a hushed interval, a recital ends and the audience bursts out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: clapping is what breaks out at the end of a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause breaks out from an audience, so it is something that erupts after a performance.

clue.text: Stories about King making responses on social media

clue.text: Space programme's latest? Look amazed

clue.text: Religious in abundance, but dismissing heads of Catholic order

clue.text: One of the birds or bats

explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is a bird, and informally means mad, as does bats.

clue.text: Follow poster used in display

parts.note: a show is a display
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster

explanation.surface: A billboard features in an exhibition someone tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them closely and secretly.

clue.text: Speak, for example

definitions.meaning: ... introduces an example, as in ..., a dog
